source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When should an ostomy pouch be emptied?
questions.rationale: Empty the pouch when one-third full; an overly full bag can loosen the skin barrier.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Ostomy Care (PDF p. 48)
questions.quote: Empty if ostomy bag is 1/3 full.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which product should be avoided when cleaning peristomal skin?
questions.rationale: Deodorant or moisturizing soaps interfere with skin barrier adhesives.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Ostomy Care (PDF p. 48)
questions.quote: Do not use deodorant or moisturizing soaps

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When is the best time to change an ostomy appliance?
questions.rationale: Avoid times near meals, visiting hours, or after medications, which may stimulate evacuation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Ostomy Care (PDF p. 48)
questions.quote: Avoid times immediately after meals or the administration of any medications

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which urine specific gravity is normal?
questions.rationale: Normal specific gravity is 1.010–1.025.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urine Characteristics (PDF p. 48)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An adult's normal 24-hour urine output is about:
questions.rationale: Normal adult output is 1200–1500 mL per 24 hours.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urine Characteristics (PDF p. 48)
questions.quote: Normal: 1200-1500 ml

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Urine output under 500 mL a day in an adult is called:
questions.rationale: Oliguria is low output, usually under 500 mL/day; anuria is under 100 mL/day.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urinary Problems (PDF p. 49)
questions.quote: Oliguria- low urine output usually less than 500 ml/day

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A woman leaks a little urine when she sneezes. Which incontinence is this?
questions.rationale: Stress incontinence is leakage (under 50 mL) with increased abdominal pressure from sneezing or coughing.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urinary Incontinence (PDF p. 49)
questions.quote: Stress incontinence – leakage of less than 50 ml of urine as a result of sudden increase in intra-abdominal pressure

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Involuntary urination in children beyond what age is called enuresis?
questions.rationale: Enuresis is involuntary urination in children beyond 4–5 years old.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urinary Problems (PDF p. 49)
questions.quote: Enuresis- involuntary urination in children beyond 4-5 years old

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which catheter is used for continuous bladder irrigation?
questions.rationale: The three-way Foley has a third lumen for irrigating fluid.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urinary Catheterization (PDF p. 49)
questions.quote: Three-way Foley catheter is used for clients who requires continuous or intermittent bladder irrigation

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which catheter size is usually used for an adult female?
questions.rationale: Female Fr 12–14; male Fr 16–18.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urinary Catheter (PDF p. 50)
questions.quote: Female: Fr. 12-14

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During female catheterization, the catheter slips into the vagina. What should the nurse do?
options: Pull it out and reinsert it
Leave it and insert a new sterile catheter
Use the same catheter after wiping
questions.rationale: Leave it in the vagina as a landmark and insert a new sterile catheter into the meatus.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urinary Catheter (PDF p. 50)
questions.quote: If the catheter accidentally slips into vagina, leave it there until new catheter is inserted in the meatus

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How is the penis held during male catheter insertion?
questions.rationale: Holding the penis perpendicular (90°) straightens the urethra.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urinary Catheter (PDF p. 50)
questions.quote: hold the penis at 90 degree angle or perpendicular to the body

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How much urine is drained at a time when relieving a distended bladder?
questions.rationale: Gradual decompression of 750–1000 mL at a time prevents shock.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urinary Catheter (PDF p. 50)
questions.quote: Only 750-1000ml of urine are to be drained at a time

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Where is a male's indwelling catheter anchored?
questions.rationale: Anchoring on the lower abdomen prevents penoscrotal pressure; females are anchored on the inner thigh.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urinary Catheter (PDF p. 50)
questions.quote: Male: laterally or upward over the lower abdomen to prevent penoscrotal pressure

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After Foley removal, within how many hours should the client void?
questions.rationale: Voiding is expected within 6–8 hours; if not by 8 hours, assess for retention.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Removal of Catheter (PDF p. 50)
questions.quote: Voiding should be expected within 6-8 hours from the time of removal of the catheter

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: From which end is a stretcher pushed?
questions.rationale: Push from the head end to protect the client's head in a collision.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Safe Use of Stretcher (PDF p. 50)
questions.quote: Always push a stretcher from the end where the client’s head in the positioned.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How is the wheelchair placed for a client who has difficulty walking?
options: At a 45° angle to the bed
questions.rationale: A 45° angle lets the client pivot into the chair with less rotation; wheels are locked.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bed to Wheelchair Transfer (PDF p. 51)
questions.quote: place the wheelchair at a 45-degree angle to the bed

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A wife grieves for months before her ailing husband dies. This is:
questions.rationale: Anticipatory grief is experienced before the loss occurs.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Grief (PDF p. 52)
questions.quote: Anticipatory grief — experienced in advance of the event

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A woman cannot openly grieve a loss society disapproves of. This is:
questions.rationale: Disenfranchised grief occurs when the loss cannot be disclosed, often a socially unacceptable loss.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Grief (PDF p. 52)
questions.quote: Disenfranchised grief — occurs when a person is unable to disclose the loss to other persons

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Grief suppressed for a long time and expressed much later is:
questions.rationale: Delayed grief occurs when feelings are suppressed until a much later time.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Complicated Grief (PDF p. 52)
questions.quote: Delayed grief - occurs when feelings are purposely or subconsciously suppressed until a much later time

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A client in the denial stage acts falsely cheerful. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: In denial, the nurse supports the client verbally but does not reinforce denial.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Kubler-Ross Stages (PDF p. 52)
questions.quote: Verbally support client but do not reinforce denial

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A dying client is angry at the nurse over small matters. What is BEST?
questions.rationale: Help the client see anger as a normal response to loss; avoid withdrawal or retaliation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Kubler-Ross Stages (PDF p. 52)
questions.quote: Avoid withdrawal or retaliation

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: In the depression stage of grief, what helps MOST?
questions.rationale: Allow sadness, communicate nonverbally by sitting quietly, and convey caring by touch.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Kubler-Ross Stages (PDF p. 53)
questions.quote: Communicate nonverbally by sitting quietly without expecting conversation

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which is a sign of impending death from loss of muscle tone?
questions.rationale: Loss of muscle tone includes facial relaxation (sagging jaw), difficulty swallowing, and incontinence.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Signs of Impending Death (PDF p. 53)
questions.quote: Relaxation of the facial muscles (e.g., the jaw may sag)
